## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Kaṇhajātaka* (Ja 29), translated into English as *The Bull Named Black*, is a short tale preserved in the Pali *Jātaka* collection [SuttaCentral]. According to the narrative framework preserved in its blurb, the Buddha recounted this past-life story while staying at the Jetavana monastery in connection with the Double Miracle, an episode noted as being treated alongside the Descent from Heaven in the thirteenth book's *Sarabhamigajātaka* [SuttaCentral]. The core verse opens with the phrase "With heavy loads" [SuttaCentral].

No Pali-internal text reuse or cross-language parallels in Sanskrit, Chinese, or Tibetan are identified for this Jātaka in SuttaCentral or DharmaNexus [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. Mention of a *Kaṇha-jātaka* in modern secondary literature typically refers to the later, homonymous story of the dark-complexioned ascetic Kaṇha (Ja 440) or to the medieval Tantric master Kāṇha, rather than this text. The Jātaka has been translated into several modern languages, with SuttaCentral recording seven translations across five languages, including an English version by Bhikkhu Sujato [SuttaCentral].
